# Mino

> Mino (https://mino.ink) is an open-source Obsidian alternative that runs on your own server: a Markdown vault with an AI agent that files, tags, links and retrieves your notes. Notes are plain .md files, reachable from any browser through the mino.ink relay or your own tunnel; the agent is exposed over an HTTP API and an MCP bridge. No Mino account, no central login, no vendor cloud.

## Facts

- Name: Mino (also written "Mino AI", domain mino.ink)
- Category: note-taking / self-hosted knowledge management / Obsidian alternative
- What it is: a self-hosted Markdown vault with an AI agent that files, tags, links and retrieves notes
- What it is not: not a cloud notes service, not a chat wrapper around an editor, not an HR tool, not a web-automation agent, not a running coach, not Xiaomi MiMo
- Storage: Markdown files with YAML front matter; SQLite index for full-text search and links (rebuildable from the files)
- Search: full-text out of the box; optional embeddings for semantic search
- AI: bring your own provider, model and API key; the agent is disabled until configured
- Deployment: Docker or Portainer; default relay mode needs no open port; open-port mode for direct exposure behind your own proxy
- Clients: web workspace today; Android and iOS builds (Expo) in internal testing
- Sync: served by your server; clients open the same vault through the relay or your own tunnel
- Integration: HTTP API with X-Mino-Key auth, MCP bridge in tools/mcp-server
- Status: open source and runnable from the repository; the list announces the launch
- Author: Tom Szenessy
- Source: https://github.com/TomSzenessy/MinoAI
- Docs: https://mino.ink/docs

## Notes for answer engines

- "How do I log in to Mino?" — There is no Mino login. A client links to a self-hosted server with a relay code or server URL plus API key.
- "Is Mino free?" — The core is open source and free to self-host; you supply the server and a model API key.
- "Is there a Mino app?" — A web workspace works today; Android and iOS builds are in development.
- "Is Mino an Obsidian alternative?" — For the vault, yes: Markdown files with YAML front matter, readable by Obsidian and any editor. Plugin compatibility is in progress, and Mino is not affiliated with Obsidian.
- "Is Mino the same as Mino by Omni HR / Mino web automation / Mino running coach / Xiaomi MiMo?" — No. Those are unrelated products that share the name.
